findings.text: blocking: the lookup hardcodes crew_home()/session-hosts while the host writes through session_host._state_dir(), which honors RECKON_SESSION_HOST_STATE_DIR; with that override a live host is missed and the hook still advises a duplicate reckon crew follow.

follow-on: the planted host pid equals the owner pid, so the new assertion would still pass if the hook ignored the record's pid and used the owner instead; use a separate live process to guard the distinct-host identity.

item_verdicts.diff: commit 0883fd5ed7ef against base 3ff8058dd3d89d35b5ea4d7341be65d2f6f412bb adds host-record lookup and branches in reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:388-410 and :805-813 plus live-host and dead-host assertions in the two named test files.
item_verdicts.done_when: the source brief names both host cases and the focused gate; after-hook-tests.log records 39 passed and EXIT=0, while reproduction.log shows both cases red at the base and negative-control.log shows the no-snapshot case red without the guard.
item_verdicts.goal: the source brief requires live-host guidance for no snapshot and stale snapshot; reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:805-813 names the host and next-dispatch re-arm in both branches, except when the host record is moved by its supported override.
item_verdicts.manifest: the source manifest names complete status, commit 0883fd5ed7ef, the three changed paths, baseline-hook-tests.log with one timeout failure, and after-hook-tests.log with zero failures; the opened logs agree.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source brief and manifest declare reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py and the two named test files; git show 0883fd5ed7ef lists exactly those three paths.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_missing_snapshot_names_a_live_seat.py:191-196 and tests/test_a_stale_snapshot_names_its_remedy.py:215-220 redden if the host remedy is removed, while :209 reddens if a dead host is treated as live; the tests do not challenge the host-record directory override or a host pid distinct from its owner.
justifications.evidence: after-hook-tests.log records 39 passed EXIT=0 and reproduction.log plus negative-control.log show the host-remedy assertions failing with the old behavior, while baseline-hook-tests.log's one failure is a git-worktree timeout outside the changed code.
justifications.fit: reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:388-410 follows the hook's snapshot-module loading style and adds no forbidden name, but :397 bypasses the session host's state-directory resolver at reckon/crew/session_host.py:117-123.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:805-813 changes both requested remedies, but :397 misses a live host whose owner put its census under RECKON_SESSION_HOST_STATE_DIR.
justifications.reuse: reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:397 duplicates the host-record path capability owned by reckon/crew/session_host.py:117-123 and already consumed through reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:515-531 rather than extending that owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show 0883fd5ed7ef names only reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py and the two test files declared in the source brief.
